objective_definitions.articulability: Prompt-based operationalization: an LLM prompt produces the articulated judgement or extraction. Prompt repeatability is evidence about this channel, not a code certificate.
objective_definitions.verifiability: Code-based operationalization: an executed, scoped program checks a relation and can emit coverage, abstention, counterexamples, or a replayable certificate.
objective_definitions.isomorphic_reconstruction: Agreement of a prompt, code, or hybrid program with the frozen LLM reference instrument on the same represented evidence. Agreement is descriptive unless the reference was sealed during discovery.
objective_definitions.constructive_extension: A code-native invariant or execution result that directly adjudicates a relation even when it disagrees with, or is unavailable to, the LLM reference. Correlation alone never establishes extension.

cases.relation: whether a stated hypothesis licenses the subsequent mathematical operation

limitations: The corpus is Math.SE question-and-answer prose, not a formal proof corpus.
Most licensing relations are condition-to-operation statements; the available SymPy operation checks equation-to-equation consequences.

artifacts.role: manually supplied SymPy-backed capability library used by the historical cell
agent-authored integration of the supplied capability
frozen relation probes and corpus-coverage replay

utility.claim: The selected seed demonstrates useful formal discrimination on its equation-equivalence subrelation and exposes a precise scope mismatch: zero real a150 licensing occurrences enter that solver relation.
limitations: Utility is diagnostic and subrelation-local; it does not verify the full a150 condition-to-operation construct.

articulability.claim: The two prompt realizations for a150 are reasonably repeatable; this describes prompt articulability and does not validate the mathematical relation independently.
limitations: Same-family prompt repeatability is not a code certificate.

verifiability.claim: The SymPy checker distinguishes the hand-built genuine and wrong algebraic consequents, but it abstains on every real structurally located a150 licensing occurrence.
limitations: Synthetic relation probes were authored during the historical workflow.
Zero real coverage means no corpus-level verifiability result for a150.

isomorphic_reconstruction.claim: The replay candidate improved train agreement with the visible LLM reference, but the historical report attributes that gain to bookkeeping and anti-laundering changes rather than the zero-coverage SymPy operation.
limitations: This is adaptive train agreement, not a sealed-reference confirmation.
The candidate changed more than capability availability.

constructive_extension.claim: The code-native algebra check is a candidate extension mechanism on synthetic probes, but no real-corpus a150 instance was certified and no verifier-adjudicated LLM disagreement was measured.
limitations: A synthetic capability test is not evidence that code extends the target relation on this corpus.

cases.relation: whether a diff supplies tests that pin the changed behavior

relation_depth.label: environment_or_world_execution
relation_depth.mechanism: repository/test-transition execution payload exposed through a mocked lookup

limitations: The program consumes a lookup of previously computed transitions; it does not execute repositories live.
The ordinary code-review corpus is diff-only. Repository state exists only in this mocked replay lane.

utility.claim: The selected mock pipeline contributes runtime evidence and improves reconstruction over its no-execution twin, while high indeterminacy and a stronger text baseline bound its present utility.
limitations: Utility is conditional on the frozen mocked execution payload.

articulability.claim: The test-adequacy prompt reference is highly repeatable in the historical replay.
limitations: Repeatability does not show that the prompt observed executed test behavior.

verifiability.claim: The frozen payload contains executable transition classes, but most attempted replays are indeterminate and the current op is a lookup rather than a live verifier.
limitations: Mock lookup provenance prevents a live-execution claim.

isomorphic_reconstruction.claim: Mock execution adds a positive marginal against the frozen LLM reference, but the full hybrid remains far below the frozen text-only baseline.
limitations: The decomposition was manually constructed and the reference was not sealed during discovery.

constructive_extension.claim: Within the selected mock pipeline, execution supplies assertion-failure evidence unavailable to a text-only prompt; this is a provenance-conditioned evidence extension, not proof that the historical selector discovered it automatically.
limitations: Presence of runtime evidence does not by itself establish that it correctly overturns an LLM judgement.

cases.relation: whether retrieved prior-art disclosures anticipate at least one claim

relation_depth.label: formal_solver_or_evidence_graph
relation_depth.mechanism: claim-to-prior-art evidence graph with deterministic aggregation over oracle-conditioned disclosure records

limitations: The base patent corpus contains abstract and claims, not specifications.
Candidate prior-art evidence is examiner/privileged injected and must not be interpreted as autonomous prior-art discovery.
Disclosure verdicts in the payload include an LLM-reading stage; deterministic aggregation is not pure code verification.

artifacts.role: prior-art evidence interface over privileged candidates and LLM disclosure verdicts

utility.claim: The selected oracle seed demonstrates that evidence-aligned claim checking has large utility for reconstructing an evidence-aware prompt reference, even though it does not demonstrate autonomous retrieval.
limitations: Utility is conditional on privileged candidate prior art and an LLM disclosure stage.

articulability.claim: Supplying the same prior-art payload to the prompt changes the articulated target and yields moderate prompt repeatability for a34.
limitations: This is an evidence-aware prompt target, not the original document-only prompt target.

verifiability.claim: The program deterministically aggregates claim-level disclosure records, but the records are oracle-conditioned and include LLM disclosure judgements, so this is a hybrid evidence process rather than pure code verification.
limitations: No autonomous retrieval or specification-level claim chart is demonstrated.

isomorphic_reconstruction.claim: Conditioned on the same oracle evidence surface, the manual hybrid strongly reconstructs the evidence-aware LLM reference and substantially exceeds its no-op twin.
limitations: This is oracle-conditioned reconstruction, not autonomous evidence discovery.
The reference was not sealed during decomposition, so the result remains retrospective rather than confirmatory.

constructive_extension.claim: No code-native certificate was used to adjudicate disagreements with the evidence-aware LLM reference.
limitations: Oracle evidence and an LLM disclosure stage cannot support an unconditioned code-beats-LLM claim.

cases.relation: whether an abstract makes a grounded code/data release claim

relation_depth.label: parsed_document_structure
relation_depth.mechanism: URL parsing plus containment grounding within the abstract

limitations: The current peer-review corpus contains abstracts rather than full papers.
URL grounding can check that a release claim is stated, not that the repository exists or reproduces results.

artifacts.role: manual URL parsing and prompt-extraction hybrid

utility.claim: The selected abstract-only seed does not improve reconstruction in its small historical subset and cannot check repository existence or result reproduction.
limitations: Only ten historical items are scoreable.

articulability.claim: The release-claim prompt has only moderate repeatability in the small scoreable subset.
limitations: The evaluation has only ten scoreable items.

verifiability.claim: A URL parser and text-containment guard exist, but no frozen relation-level certificate suite establishes verifiability.
limitations: Program existence is not a verifier certificate.

isomorphic_reconstruction.claim: The manual hybrid does not improve reconstruction of the frozen LLM reference in the small historical subset.
limitations: The small scoreable subset makes this a weak negative.

constructive_extension.claim: Abstract-only inputs cannot certify repository availability or reproducibility, so no constructive extension is evaluated.
limitations: Repository snapshots and executable environments are absent.

cases.relation: whether the full-paper results section supports the abstract's headline claim

relation_depth.label: cross_span_or_section_relation
relation_depth.mechanism: abstract claim extraction followed by body/results evidence matching

limitations: The current peer-review items contain abstracts only.
The existing claim-support program expects a body/results section and must abstain rather than treat the abstract as its own evidence.

utility.claim: The selected claim/body decomposition is useful in principle but cannot execute on the historical abstract-only evidence surface.
limitations: The selected pipeline requires results-body evidence.

articulability.claim: No body-conditioned prompt target is present in this corpus.
limitations: Results-body evidence is absent.

verifiability.claim: The relation cannot be executed because the required results body is absent.
limitations: The verifier must abstain rather than self-match the abstract.

isomorphic_reconstruction.claim: No isomorphic reconstruction comparison is defined on mismatched evidence surfaces.
limitations: Prompt and verifier would not see the required common evidence.

constructive_extension.claim: No code-native extension is possible without full-paper evidence.
limitations: A future full-paper corpus is required.

cases.relation: whether transplanted tests behaviorally pin, partially pin, or vacuously pass the changed code

relation_depth.label: environment_or_world_execution
relation_depth.mechanism: stored telemetry produced by prior repository checkout, test transplant, and execution in era-matched containers; current replay performs classification only

limitations: Only a minority of rows produce decisive pinned/partial/vacuous certificates; most are indeterminate or abstain.
The consolidated file contains one duplicated row identifier with conflicting non-certificate labels; counts are reported on all 800 rows and the duplicate is disclosed.
Historical accept/reject columns are present in the source but ignored by the replay probe.

artifacts.role: legacy prototype report for executions completed before the current replay
frozen 800-row telemetry artifact from prior transplant executions
unsupervised certificate-coverage probe that ignores accept/reject fields
resolved execution coverage and integrity readout

utility.claim: The selected legacy prototype artifact contains 65 direct behavioral transition certificates across three languages; the current replay classifies frozen telemetry rather than launching executions, and reports low coverage rather than hiding it.
limitations: Certificate coverage is 8.1%, so the pipeline is an abstaining specialist rather than a universal metric.

articulability.claim: This selected case evaluates executable test transitions, not a new prompt program.
limitations: The frozen historical prompt reconstruction remains in the separate a104 mock-replay case.

verifiability.claim: Frozen telemetry from prior repository/test execution supplies scoped pinned, partial-pinned, and vacuous transition certificates with explicit abstention and error classes; no repository executes in this replay.
limitations: A certificate is available on 65 of 800 rows; indeterminate is not treated as failure.

isomorphic_reconstruction.claim: No new LLM-reference reconstruction statistic is computed from the 800-row artifact; the source accept/reject field is ignored.
limitations: This case reports the certificate plane only.

constructive_extension.claim: Behavioral test transitions extend the represented evidence beyond diff text: execution can certify pinning or vacuity even when prompt isomorphism is unavailable or imperfect.
limitations: This is an executable-evidence extension, not a claim that every execution verdict supersedes an LLM judgement.

cases.relation: whether a conservatively normalized numeric token in the abstract recurs in extracted methods/results/evaluation body text

relation_depth.label: cross_span_or_section_relation
relation_depth.mechanism: section-targeted full-paper evidence plus conservative abstract-to-body numeric recurrence

limitations: Full-paper evidence is PDF-section extraction and can omit, duplicate, or corrupt content.
Positive exact recurrence is a narrow certificate; zero recurrence remains unresolved because values may be reformatted, converted, or paraphrased.
The source contains a historical accept/reject y field, but the new probe never reads it.
Generated full-paper/abstract code-score NPZs referenced by historical scripts are absent locally, so no NPZ-derived reconstruction result is asserted.

artifacts.role: historical full-paper LLM-field extraction script; generated fields unavailable locally
historical matched abstract-vs-full-paper NPZ comparator; referenced NPZs unavailable locally
historical prompt-extract then code-verify scoring design; NPZ output unavailable locally
unlabelled cross-section recurrence and coverage probe

utility.claim: Selecting the full-paper evidence surface makes the intended cross-section verifier executable: 1,957 papers have body evidence and 429 receive positive numeric-recurrence certificates without consulting outcome labels.
limitations: Utility is evidence coverage and certificate yield, not accept/reject prediction.

articulability.claim: The available full-paper artifacts do not include a locally replayable frozen full-paper prompt-judgement result.
limitations: Historical field-extraction scripts exist, but their generated field and NPZ outputs are absent locally.

verifiability.claim: Code issues conservative positive certificates when normalized specific numeric claims recur across abstract and body, while abstaining on absent bodies, nonnumeric claims, and zero matches.
limitations: The certificate establishes recurrence, not semantic support, causal validity, or correctness of the result.

isomorphic_reconstruction.claim: No frozen full-paper LLM-reference reconstruction comparison is available locally, and accept/reject outcomes are not substituted for it.
limitations: This selected case currently reports the certificate plane rather than the reference plane.

constructive_extension.claim: Full-paper access extends the abstract-only pipeline by making cross-section evidence recurrence executable; 429 positive certificates use information the abstract-only prompt could not inspect.
limitations: This is an evidence-surface extension, not a verified claim that the LLM reference is wrong.
